# THE WINDOWS TEST SHARDS (U-ci-shards) — the partition, here and nowhere else. Read only by
# .github/ci/shard-filter.sh: the workflow makes one windows test job per shard, and each runs the whole
# solution outside the Timing category under that shard's filter.
#
# "shards N" says how many. Every other line is "<shard> <fully qualified test class>", for shards 1 to N-1;
# shard N, the LAST, lists nothing and runs every test of a class listed nowhere — so a new class, or one
# renamed, runs there by construction and no test is ever left out. A class on two lines (in any case) is
# refused; a listed class that ran no test in its shard is a ::warning on the run, meaning a stale line.
#
# BALANCED ON WINDOWS ALONE, from the summed test durations of run 38046993760 (the three assemblies on one
# runner, so the figures are inflated, and their sum is what was balanced). Fault and Integration run their
# tests one at a time, so a shard lasts about as long as the larger of its Fault and Integration sums; Unit runs
# its classes in parallel. Shard 1 is kept light because it also runs the whole Timing category, about ten
# minutes. Rebalance by moving lines; the comment above each shard is that run's sums, not a check.

shards 5

# shard 1: Fault 71 s, Integration 0 s, Unit 0 s — then the Timing category, every test of it
